name: Longer Ray7 15W
tagline: The value Ray7: a 15W diode that engraves sharply and cuts thin plywood, for under $300
tldr: The Ray7 15W sits one step above the entry model at $299.99 on Longer's store (October 2026). It keeps a fine 0.06 × 0.08 mm spot for detail while cutting 3 mm basswood in a single pass by our estimate, on the same 405 × 410 mm open frame with Wi-Fi and 600 mm/s motion. For hobbyists who engrave most of the time and cut boxes or ornaments now and then, it is the best-balanced price in the range.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving with light cutting of 3–5 mm wood, at a hobby budget

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood 3 mm in one pass, ~5 mm with air (our estimate)

pros: Still a fine 0.06 × 0.08 mm spot according to Longer, close to the entry module for photos
Cuts 3 mm basswood in one pass and about 5 mm with air assist by our estimate
$299.99 in October 2026, only $70 more than the entry Ray7 for roughly twice the cutting capacity

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 15W version of the Longer Ray7. It suits buyers who engrave most of the time and cut ornaments, coasters and small boxes in 3 mm wood. Compare the other Ray7 versions with the chips above if you plan regular cuts above 6 mm. The frame, bed and software are the same across the range.
proTips: Add the air pump before cutting: it keeps edges cleaner and lets you raise the speed. Run a test grid on each new plywood batch, as glue layers vary. For photos, slow the fill and lower the power slightly to keep the narrow spot sharp.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 15W is the sweet spot of the Ray7 range on price: it keeps a fine spot for detailed engraving and cuts the 3 mm stock most hobby projects use, for a little under $300 with a full-size bed and Wi-Fi.
editorialDepth.limitations: Thicker plywood and dark acrylic need many passes; buyers who cut every week will outgrow it. Open frame: safety glasses and smoke extraction are required. No independent tests of the Ray7 yet, so speed and reliability figures rest on Longer's data and our estimates.

faq.question: How thick can the Ray7 15W cut?
faq.answer: Longer does not publish per-version cutting figures. By our estimate it cuts 3 mm basswood in one pass, about 5 mm with air assist, and 6 mm plywood in several passes. Dense hardwoods and MDF cut slower.

faq.question: Ray7 15W or Ray7 20W?
faq.answer: The 20W costs $429.99 against $299.99 for the 15W (Longer store, October 2026). The $130 step buys faster cuts and better results on 5–8 mm wood; if you mostly engrave, the 15W keeps a finer spot and the savings can pay for the air pump.

faq.question: Is an air pump needed on the Ray7 15W?
faq.answer: For engraving, no. For cutting, it is strongly recommended: it clears smoke from the cut, reduces scorching and allows higher speeds. Longer sells it as an option for this version.
